title: Replit CEO's surprising take:  AI is making software engineering more human
excerpt: Replit CEO Amjad Masad said his company's office has become "more vibrant" since his software engineers started vibe coding.
content_html:
Replit CEO Amjad Masad says AI is making software engineering at his company more cerebral and fun.

That's a surprising take, given the widespread concern about the so-called "SaaSpocalypse" and fears that AI is replacing coding jobs at software companies.

Speaking on tech journalist Casey Newton's podcast, Masad said coding agents have changed the day-to-day environment at his company, freeing up engineers for more imaginative tasks.

"You are trying a lot of things, you are ideating very quickly," Masad said. "Two years ago, everyone is hands on keyboard, you hear clicking all the time."

"Now, actually, it's a lot more vibrant environment," he added.

Others, too, have scoffed at the idea that AI could spell the end of the software industry. Jared Spataro, a Microsoft executive overseeing marketing for AI-powered workplace tools, earlier told Business Insider that he thinks that "the rumors of the demise of enterprise software are greatly exaggerated."

Investors, meanwhile, have not been so buoyant. The notion that AI could let companies build their own software — instead of contracting the work out to dedicated software builders, like Microsoft — rattled the markets earlier this year.

Software engineers themselves have said that coding with AI, while more efficient, quickly leads to burnout, and at least a dozen major companies have laid off workers, citing AI as a reason.

This summer, Meta laid off nearly 1,000 software engineers. Mark Zuckerberg, however, attributed the cuts to the need to offset AI spending rather than to automation itself.

Masad said that Replit, an integrated coding environment he cofounded in 2016, reached an inflection point in 2025 when Anthropic began releasing its Opus models. The models could write code more effectively than earlier ones.

"My entire life mission around teaching people coding and making coding easier is changing," Masad recalled thinking at the time. "Everything that I work toward is kind of moot."

Masad said Replit adapted by shifting its mission from teaching people how to code to making coding as easy as possible. The company built an AI agent to build programs from requests made in plain English, a process now known as vibe coding.

Now, he said, Replit's engineers spend more time at the whiteboard, taking occasional breaks to send the next prompt to an AI agent.

"You create a culture where it's fun to build things," Masad said. "You create a culture where it's not intense all the time."

content_html_zh:
Replit 首席执行官 Amjad Masad 表示，人工智能正在让他公司的软件工程变得更加理智和有趣。

考虑到人们对所谓的“SaaS 末日”的广泛担忧以及人工智能正在取代软件公司的编码工作的担忧，这是一个令人惊讶的做法。

马萨德在科技记者 Casey Newton 的播客中表示，编码代理改变了他公司的日常环境，使工程师能够腾出时间来完成更具想象力的任务。

“你正在尝试很多事情，你的想法很快，”马萨德说。 “两年前，每个人都把手放在键盘上，你总是听到咔哒声。”

“实际上，现在的环境更加充满活力，”他补充道。

其他人也嘲笑人工智能可能导致软件行业终结的想法。 微软负责人工智能工作场所工具营销的高管贾里德·斯帕塔罗(Jared Spataro)早些时候告诉《商业内幕》，他认为“企业软件消亡的传言被严重夸大了”。

与此同时，投资者却没有那么乐观。 今年早些时候，人工智能可以让公司构建自己的软件——而不是把工作外包给微软等专门的软件开发者——的想法震惊了市场。

软件工程师自己也表示，用人工智能编码虽然效率更高，但很快就会导致倦怠，至少有十几家大公司以人工智能为理由解雇了员工。

今年夏天，Meta 解雇了近 1000 名软件工程师。 然而，马克扎克伯格将削减归因于抵消人工智能支出的需要，而不是自动化本身。

Masad 表示，他于 2016 年共同创立的集成编码环境 Replit 在 2025 年达到了拐点，当时 Anthropic 开始发布其 Opus 模型。 这些模型可以比早期的模型更有效地编写代码。

“我一生的使命是教人们编码并让编码变得更容易，这一使命正在改变，”马萨德回忆起当时的想法。 “我所做的一切努力都是毫无意义的。”

Masad 表示，Replit 进行了调整，将其使命从教人们如何编码转变为让编码尽可能简单。 该公司构建了一个人工智能代理，可以根据简单英语的请求构建程序，这一过程现在被称为“vibe 编码”。

他说，现在，Replit 的工程师在白板上花费了更多的时间，偶尔休息一下，将下一个提示发送给人工智能代理。

“你创造了一种创造事物的乐趣的文化，”马萨德说。 “你创造了一种并不总是很激烈的文化。”
